comparison: Perfect agreement on the main finding (C21, C29, C52). Both evaluations strongly support the hierarchical gradient of background invariance across auditory cortex. OpenEval cites specific statistical evidence (p≤0.001, Figures 2E-F), while peer reviewers provide qualitative affirmation describing it as 'convincing evidence' and 'important replication.'

Perfect agreement on experimental design and basic response properties (C24-C28). Both evaluations support the methodological approach. OpenEval provides technical validation (stationarity-based classification, cross-correlation analysis in Figure 1E), while peer reviewers affirm the study is 'well conducted' with 'clear presentation.'

Perfect agreement on species differences (C23, C51, C54-C55, C61). Both evaluations support the finding that the model explains less variance in humans than ferrets. OpenEval provides quantitative details (r=0.23±0.04 vs r=0.65±0.007, p=0.0167) and notes the conclusion about 'additional mechanisms' is inferential. Peer reviewers accept the finding without challenge, describing conclusions as 'well supported.'

Strong agreement on modeling results (C22, C43, C53 overlap). Both evaluations support the spectrotemporal model's explanatory power. OpenEval details technical achievements (noise-corrected r=0.65±0.007, tonotopic organization, Figure 4D p≤0.05). Peer reviewers praise the 'elegance of modeling' and describe it as a 'compelling framework' using 'well-established' methods.

Partial overlap on acoustic analysis (C34-C35 in OpenEval; C34-C37 in peer review). Both evaluations support the acoustic characterization and modeling. OpenEval focuses on temporal modulation discrimination (Figures 3B-C), while peer review also encompasses broader modeling aspects (C36-C37), affirming 'clear and well supported' quantification.

Minimal overlap on model predictive accuracy (C40 only). Both evaluations support the model's performance. OpenEval provides comprehensive technical validation across multiple claims (C22, C36-C37, C40, C43, C53), while peer review R6 focuses specifically on C40, describing the model as 'well-established' and 'appropriate.'

Partial overlap on primary cortex findings (C56-C57). OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN, noting C56 is supported by data (p=0.063 ferrets, p=0.577 humans) but C57 is 'purely speculative' about functional roles. Peer reviewers are more accepting, noting the complementary foreground invariance analysis without challenging the functional speculation.

Strong overlap on methodological considerations (C62-C64). OpenEval rates these UNCERTAIN, noting 'somewhat circular' reasoning and lack of quantitative evidence for ruling out confounds. Peer reviewers are more accepting, confirming 'authors have addressed all points raised' and expressing satisfaction with how methodological issues were handled.

Strong overlap on discussion of species differences (C65-C71). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes they are 'appropriately presented as speculative possibilities' with important acknowledged limitations (C66, C65). Peer reviewers accept these as 'reasonable discussion points' without challenge, affirming the work's interest to the research community.

Partial overlap on limitations (C65-C66). OpenEval discusses these as part of broader alternative explanations (C65-C71), noting lack of behavioral validation and task confounds. Peer review R8 groups these with methodological considerations (C62-C66), accepting the authors' treatment of limitations.

Partial overlap on background literature (C1, C5-C9). OpenEval evaluates these as SUPPORTED foundational context from prior human studies. Peer review R10 encompasses broader literature framing (C1-C20), accepting the background without challenge and confirming the study provides 'important replication' that 'extends original findings.'

Partial overlap on knowledge gap identification (C10-C14, C20). OpenEval supports these claims as appropriately identifying gaps in hierarchical organization evidence. Peer review R10 encompasses this within broader literature acceptance (C1-C20), affirming the motivation and framing as valid.

Partial overlap on mechanistic hypotheses (C15-C19). OpenEval supports these claims with appropriate citations, noting speculative aspects (C17, C19) are properly qualified. Peer review R10 includes these in broader literature acceptance (C1-C20), confirming the study 'extends original findings in three ways.'

OpenEval evaluates extensive methodological details (C75-C87) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate noise-correction, ridge regression, and permutation tests, while acknowledging small sample size (n=3 ferrets). No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers generally affirm the study is 'well conducted.'

OpenEval evaluates foreground/background sound definitions (C2-C4) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though these foundational concepts are implicitly accepted in peer reviewers' overall affirmation of the study.

OpenEval evaluates citations about contradictory ferret hierarchy findings (C72-C73) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of complexity. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for these particular literature contextualization claims.
